# 单篇讲义生成任务

项目仓库: typst/typst
项目名: typst
讲义目录: typst-tutorial/
代码永久链接 base: https://github.com/typst/typst/blob/84cca406aafe7f830ed3f37f1cc6f0c8b6b65a03/
当前 HEAD: 84cca406aafe7f830ed3f37f1cc6f0c8b6b65a03
动作: new


---

## 项目学习路线（大纲方法论）

# 项目学习手册·大纲规划 Planner

## 角色

你是资深技术教育专家、源码阅读导师和项目学习路线设计者。

你运行在被分析项目的根目录内。

你可以使用：

- `Read`
- `Grep`
- `Glob`
- 只读 `git` 命令，例如 `git log`、`git diff`、`git show`、`git ls-files`

你不能：

- 修改源码
- 写入任何 `.md` 文件
- 输出 JSON 以外的文字

你的唯一产出是一个学习手册大纲 manifest JSON。

---

## 总目标

为当前项目规划一套「从零开始、由浅入深、结合源码和代码实践」的学习手册。

这套手册会被拆分成多篇 Markdown 讲义，后续 worker 会根据 manifest 逐篇生成。

每篇讲义应该满足：

1. 面向初学者也能读懂。
2. 只讲一个相对独立的主题。
3. 必须结合真实源码。
4. 必须包含一个可操作的代码实践任务。
5. 讲义之间有清晰依赖关系。

---

## 源码探查顺序

请按以下顺序理解项目，不要一开始就深入细节：

1. 项目说明
   - README
   - docs
   - examples
   - tutorials

2. 构建与运行方式
   - package.json
   - Cargo.toml
   - pyproject.toml
   - go.mod
   - pom.xml
   - Makefile
   - Dockerfile
   - CI 配置

3. 项目入口
   - CLI 入口
   - Web 服务入口
   - main 文件
   - library export 文件
   - examples 入口

4. 目录结构
   - src
   - lib
   - app
   - packages
   - crates
   - tests

5. 核心流程
   - 初始化流程
   - 配置加载
   - 请求/任务/数据处理主链路
   - 插件、扩展、调度、存储等核心机制

6. 测试与示例
   - 单元测试
   - 集成测试
   - benchmark
   - example usage

---

## 学习路线设计原则

请把学习手册设计成三层：

1. 入门层 beginner
   目标：让读者知道项目是什么、怎么运行、目录如何组织、核心入口在哪里。

2. 进阶层 intermediate
   目标：让读者理解主要模块、核心调用链、关键数据结构和配置机制。

3. 专家层 advanced
   目标：让读者理解扩展点、性能、并发、错误处理、测试、二次开发和架构取舍。

---

## 讲义拆分规则

- 每篇讲义只解决一个主要问题。
- 每篇讲义包含 2 到 5 个最小模块。
- 每篇讲义必须有一个 `practice_task`，描述读者要完成的代码实践。
- 每篇讲义的源码范围要适中，通常引用 1 到 6 个关键源码文件。
- 大型项目可以拆成 30 篇以上讲义；中型项目 15 到 30 篇；小型项目 8 到 15 篇。
- 不要为了数量硬拆，逻辑优先。
- 第一单元必须帮助读者从零开始，包括项目定位、运行方式、目录结构、入口文件。
- 后续单元再进入核心模块、源码机制、扩展实践。

---

## mode=full

首次生成大纲时：

1. 阅读项目关键文件。
2. 理解项目定位、技术栈、运行方式和核心模块。
3. 设计从零开始的学习路径。
4. 输出完整 manifest。
5. 所有讲义的 `action` 都必须是 `"new"`。

---

## mode=incremental

增量更新时：

1. 读取 stdin 中提供的现有 manifest。
2. 阅读项目中已有的 `<项目名>-tutorial/` 讲义目录，理解旧结构。
3. 使用：

   - `git diff previous_head..current_head`
   - `git log`
   - `git show`

   分析代码变化。

4. 输出更新后的完整 manifest。

每篇讲义的 `action` 按以下规则设置：

- `"keep"`
  代码变化不影响这篇讲义，无需重写。

- `"update"`
  小范围改动，例如函数重命名、参数调整、局部逻辑变化、链接行号变化。

- `"new"`
  新增功能、新增模块、新增重要机制，需要新增讲义。

- `"rebuild"`
  架构、主流程、公共接口、核心模型发生重大变化，旧讲义需要重建。

如果某篇旧讲义已经不再适合当前项目结构，可以从 manifest 中移除。

---

## manifest 输出格式

只输出严格 JSON，不要输出 Markdown，不要输出解释文字。

```json
{
  "project": "<项目名>",
  "head": "<current_head>",
  "rationale": "中文说明：为什么这样设计学习顺序、单元划分和讲义顺序。",
  "units": [
    {
      "id": "u1",
      "title": "单元标题",
      "level": "beginner",
      "order": 1,
      "lectures": [
        {
          "id": "u1-l1",
          "title": "讲义标题",
          "order": 1,
          "filename": "u1-l1-project-overview.md",
          "level": "beginner",
          "topic": "本讲义要讲什么，用 1 到 3 句中文说明。",
          "learning_goals": [
            "学习目标 1",
            "学习目标 2"
          ],
          "source_files": [
            "README.md",
            "src/main.ts"
          ],
          "minimal_modules": [
            "模块 1",
            "模块 2"
          ],
          "practice_task": "本讲义对应的代码实践任务。",
          "depends_on": [],
          "action": "new"
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

---

## 字段要求

- `project`：项目名。
- `head`：当前 git HEAD。
- `rationale`：中文，一段即可。
- `unit.id`：格式为 `u1`、`u2`、`u3`。
- `lecture.id`：格式为 `u1-l1`、`u1-l2`。
- `filename`：
  - 必须全局唯一。
  - 必须小写。
  - 使用连字符。
  - 必须以 `.md` 结尾。
  - 文件位于 `<项目名>-tutorial/` 目录下。
- `level`：
  - `"beginner"`
  - `"intermediate"`
  - `"advanced"`
- `source_files`：
  - 只能填写你实际读过或确认存在的源码文件。
  - 不要编造文件路径。
- `depends_on`：
  - 使用讲义 id。
  - 没有依赖时填写空数组。
- `action`：
  - full 模式全部为 `"new"`。
  - incremental 模式使用 `"keep"`、`"update"`、`"new"`、`"rebuild"`。

---

## 重要约束

- 只基于真实源码和项目文件规划。
- 不确定的地方写 `"待确认"`。
- 不要编造不存在的模块、命令、接口或源码文件。
- 输出必须是合法 JSON。


## 完整大纲

```json
{
  "project": "typst",
  "rationale": "Typst 是一个由 17 个 Rust crate 组成的大型 Cargo workspace，编译器按「解析(typst-syntax) → 求值(typst-eval) → 内容实现(typst-realize) → 排版(typst-layout) → 导出(typst-pdf/typst-html/typst-render/typst-svg)」的流水线组织，而所有核心类型与 World/Engine 抽象集中在 typst-library，行为被拆分到各独立 crate（见 docs/dev/architecture.md 与各 lib.rs 文档注释）。因此学习路线设计为：第一单元从零开始，先让读者装好 CLI、用 Cargo 构建编译器、看清仓库与 crate 全景、跑通第一次编译并接触 tests/ 测试体系（cargo testit）；第二单元沿数据流进入语法层，依次讲 Source/FileId、Lexer、Parser/SyntaxNode、AST/Span 与增量重解析；第三单元进入 typst-library 与 typst-eval，讲 World、Library/全局作用域、Value、Content、Func/Args、解释器主循环和 Styles/set-show 数据模型；第四单元覆盖 realize、页面/flow/inline/grid/数学排版与 introspection 两遍编译；第五单元为专家层，讲 PDF/渲染/SVG 导出、Format 多目标注册机制、typst-bundle 新格式、proc-macro 体系、typst-ide 工具、typst-kit 字体与包生态、comemo 增量编译和 WASM 插件。讲义间用 depends_on 构成 DAG，每篇只讲一个主题并配一个可在本地仓库完成的代码实践任务，用 tests/ 套件或 CLI 输出验证结果。本次增量分析（64c5e8c0..84cca406a）显示变化高度集中在 typst-syntax：node.rs 大幅重构（replace_children/update_parent/renumber_children 迁移至 reparser.rs 的 InnerNode、numberize 改为 Option<&mut Span>、InnerNode 提升为 pub(super)）、reparser.rs 重写增量策略（try_reparse 更名 try_reparse_and_renumber、新增 MarkupReparse、根节点失败时仅重编号而非全量重解析、修复嵌套重解析、不再跨语法警告重解析）、Source::detached 被移除并新增 FileId::new_for_test 与 Source::new 接受 impl Into<String>；另有 location/stack/stroke 文档改进、divider 变为 Locatable、krilla/hayro 依赖升级与 typst-pdf 新增若干 a11y 校验错误分支。据此：u2-l3（SyntaxNode 树模型仍在但方法位置与签名变化）与 u2-l4（示例中的 Source::detached 已失效、span.rs Debug 输出变化）标记 update，u2-l5（核心机制被重写）标记 rebuild；其余已生成的 u1/u3/u4-l1..l3 讲义内容不受影响标记 keep；u2-l1 与 u4-l4 之后及第五单元讲义尚未生成，保持 new，生成时按新代码（如 FileId::new_for_test）撰写。",

## 前置讲义摘要（你必须基于这些已建立的认知继续，不要重复，要承接）

### u1-l1 Typst 是什么：项目定位与语言初印象

文件尾部已完整读齐（与此前收到的片段一致，无新增内容），摘要维持不变，即上一条输出：

本讲精读仓库 README 与 docs 说明，建立项目全景：Typst 是基于标记的排版系统，目标是与 LaTeX 同样强大但更易学好用，仓库本体为编译器与 CLI。六大卖点：内置标记、灵活函数、集成脚本、数学与文献管理、增量编译、友好报错。引入的关键概念：标记语言、crate、set/show 规则、# 脚本、数学模式、compile/watch 命令及输出格式按扩展名推断；三条设计原则为一致性、可组合、增量。docs 目录是官方文档站源码工程，教程与参考内容是初学者资料入口，可由 cargo docit 本地构建。下一讲转向 Cargo workspace 与从源码构建编译器。
### u1-l2 从源码构建：Cargo workspace 与构建命令

本讲把 Typst 仓库当作一个 Rust 工程从源码构建，引入 crate、workspace、集中依赖表、profile、cargo 别名等术语。核心结论：根 Cargo.toml 是 workspace 清单而非包清单，members 纳入 17 个编译器 crate 及 docs、tests 包，default-members 指向 typst-cli，故根目录裸跑 cargo 默认只构建 CLI；共享元数据（版本 0.15.1、MSRV 1.92、edition 2024）集中声明，成员以 workspace = true 继承。依赖分三种来源：path（仓库内部 crate）、git（typst-assets、typst-dev-assets 等锁定 rev，保证可复现，首次构建需联网）、registry（crates.io）。profile 分三档：dev（依赖强制 opt-level 2）、dev-fast、release。cargo testit 与 docit 是 .cargo/config.toml 中的普通别名，分别运行 test-wrapper 集成测试与 typst-docs 文档站。常用命令为 cargo build -p typst-cli、cargo run -p typst-cli -- compile、cargo test。本讲打通克隆—构建—运行闭环，为下一讲 crate 分工全景铺路。
### u1-l3 仓库全景：17 个 crate 的分工地图

本讲梳理 Typst 仓库 17 个 crate 的分工：编译按解析→求值→realize→排版→导出五段流水线推进，数据形态依次为字符串→SyntaxNode→Content→Frame→输出字节。依赖自下而上分层：底层工具、typst-syntax、类型地基 typst-library、各阶段与导出 crate、总装 typst、应用 cli/ide/kit。核心决策「类型定义在 typst-library、行为拆到各阶段 crate」由 Routines 函数指针表落实：签名住在 library、实现在总装 crate 的 ROUTINES 表接线，形同动态链接，避免循环依赖。compile 只求值一次，循环的是排版与内省至收敛；导出器仅是总装的 dev-dependency，由使用者接线；架构文档可能滞后，以源码为准。
### u1-l4 CLI 入口：从命令行到一次编译的调用链

本讲读 typst-cli 的三个文件，追踪从命令行到一次编译的调用链。main.rs 是刻意做薄的入口：子命令各对应一个同名模块文件，全局 ARGS 用 LazyLock 惰性解析一次，dispatch 以 match 分发，退出码经线程局部变量 EXIT 中转。args.rs 用 clap 派生宏实现「数据结构即接口」：compile 与 watch 借 flatten 共享 CompileArgs，Input/Output 枚举把 stdin/stdout 与文件路径统一进类型。compile.rs 的主干是先由 CompileConfig（按 --format、输出扩展名、默认 PDF 之序推断格式与输出路径）与 SystemWorld 备好环境，再执行 compile_once：compile_and_export 调 typst::compile::<T>，以泛型参数区分产出物类型（分页文档、HTML、Bundle），导出统一收敛到 Output::write。compile_once 是被 compile 与 watch 复用的单次编译单元；SystemWorld 的实现细节留待下一讲。
### u1-l5 测试体系入门：cargo testit 与 tests/ 目录

本讲解析 Typst 行内排版引擎（typst-layout/src/inline）：段落经 collect、prepare、linebreak、finalize 四阶段流水线变成多行 Frame。collect 把文本、间距、盒子、内联公式、标签拍平成一条全文 String 与统一的 Item/Segment 序列，非文本物以 U+FFFC 占位，SpanMapper 反查源码位置；prepare 做 BiDi 分析并按方向与文字系统切 run，用 rustybuzz 整形，FontBook 的 select/select_fallback 完成字体选择与 tofu 递归回退；linebreak 借 ICU4X 断行器（中日文换用定制 CJ 断行器）与 hypher 连字典枚举候选，按 Simple 贪心或 Knuth-Plass 全局最优选点，只量宽不建帧；finalize 逐行 commit：BiDi 重排、CJK-拉丁间距与行首尾标点压缩、两步 justify、Fractional 延迟布局、条目按逻辑序排列。段落得以在 flow 的 collect 阶段提前断行，因断行仅依赖行宽。关键术语：整形、字形、簇、ShapedText、InlineElem、UAX #14。
### u4-l6 网格世界：grid、table、列表与数学布局

本讲四个模块。轨道模型：grid 与 table 语义不同，但 Synthesize 阶段都被编译成统一的 CellGrid（轨道与 gutter 交织、跨行列合并记为 Entry::Merged、内建表头表脚），共用同一 GridLayouter——「一个引擎、多个语义外壳」。尺寸协商：measure_columns 对三类 Sizing 轨道按固定次序谈判——固定轨道先解析，auto 轨道用试探布局逐格测量取最大宽度，剩余空间按份数分给 fr 轨道，不足时超标 auto 列迭代公平收缩；fr 行延迟到区域收尾才定高。列表演进：列表曾用两列网格复用引擎，2026 年 5 月起改为专用 ListLayouter 加栈布局，动机是网格行模型表达不了的 marker 与正文基线对齐；如今真正复用网格的是文献目录。数学排版：resolve_equation 产出 MathItem 树，递归布局为带 ascent/descent 的 MathFragment 片段流，MathRun 按公共基线装配成行；分数、根式、矩阵的间隙全查字体 MATH 表常量，矩阵基线对轴线而非首行。
### u4-l7 内省机制：counter、引用与两遍编译

本讲是排版管线单元的收官，讲 Typst 的内省机制与多轮编译。页码、引用目标等信息在排版完成前不存在，Typst 以不动点迭代解决：求值只执行一次，排版反复以「上一轮文档」为输入，上限五轮（MAX_ITERS），首轮为盲排（空 Introspector），不收敛仅发警告且仍产出文档。关键术语：Location 是 u128 分层哈希的元素实例身份证，跨轮稳定，区别于定位源码的 Span；Locatable 指由 `#[elem(Locatable)]` 标记、可被查询的语义元素；Tag/TagElem 由 realize 的 prepare 阶段成对生成（Start 含元素快照）并随布局写入 Frame；Introspector（paged 侧为 PagedIntrospector）从页面帧收集 Tag，建成按文档序的元素表与区间/标签/哈希索引。query 与 counter 均经 Introspect trait 执行并记入 sink，计数器把更新做成可定位元素、沿文档序回放取值。收敛判定先走 comemo 约束验证快路径，五轮耗尽后由 History 在六个 introspector 上重放生成警告；性能靠求值一次、布局整体 memoize 与 Locator 稳定哈希保障。
### u5-l1 PDF 导出：从 PagedDocument 到字节流

本讲剖析 typst-pdf：它把 PagedDocument（一叠页面帧）翻译成 PDF 字节流，全程只读，不回头触碰求值与排版。入口 pdf() 是薄门面，装配在 convert：先合并 CLI 选项与文档内 #set pdf(...) 设置并校验互斥（页面范围导出会禁用标签化），再逐页遍历 Frame，把六类 FrameItem 图元翻译给后端库 krilla；序列化、压缩与字体子集化都发生在 krilla 层，typst-pdf 只负责翻译。资源去重：字体经 comemo 记忆化跨编译缓存，图像按首见登记 span。tagged PDF 由 FrameItem::Tag(Start/End) 驱动、随绘制增量构建标签树，最终经 set_tag_tree 写入，默认开启。krilla 的校验错误被逐条翻译为带 Span 与修复 hint 的 Typst 诊断。
### u5-l2 像素与矢量：typst-render 与 typst-svg

本讲覆盖 typst-render（PNG 栅格化）与 typst-svg（SVG 序列化）两个纯消费 PagedDocument 的导出 crate。共同输入是 Frame 的六类图元（Group/Text/Shape/Image/Link/Tag），两侧遍历几乎镜像：Link 仅 SVG 渲染为链接，Tag 均忽略。栅格化按 pixel_per_pt＝ppi/72 换算画布，State 携带变换、容器变换（服务 RelativeTo::Parent 渐变，区分软硬帧）与遮罩递归；形状经 tiny-skia 先填充后描边，小字号字形走 pixglyph 亚像素位图加手工混合，图像先重采样为纹理再作图案。SVG 侧是序列化而非绘制：SVGRenderer 用 Deduplicator 去重字形、渐变、平铺与裁剪路径，字形以 symbol＋use 复用，渐变拆成源定义与带变换引用两层，数字定点化保证输出字节确定。png 的 ppi 与 svg 的 pretty 选项经 Format 元素机制与 CLI 在 resolve 合并；tests 的 render、svg stage 分别调用 render_merged 与 svg_merged，参考产物以文件和哈希两种方式存放。
### u5-l3 多目标架构：Format 注册与 HTML 导出

本讲回答「导出格式如何插入编译器」。核心结论：`Format` 是结构体而非 trait，它把一种导出格式的注册信息（格式元素、选项默认值、feature 门、规则注册函数）数据化为 `FORMAT` 常量，由导出 crate 自己定义，宿主经 `Library::builder(formats)` 注入，typst-library 因此不认识任何具体格式；装配时格式元素定义进 `std.format` 模块，再经 prelude 提升为全局名（继承 feature 门控）。关键术语：格式元素（如 `HtmlFormat`，仅供 `set` 规则配置）、`Target`（Paged/Html/Bundle，与输出类型一一对应）、`Output` trait（`target()`/`create()`）、按 (元素， 目标) 键控的 `NativeRuleMap`、汇集文档内 set 选项的 `DocumentFormatOptions`。HTML 目标与 paged 共用同一条 realize 流水线，差异仅在规则查表时分岔，产物经 convert 转为 DOM、finalize_dom 收尾后序列化输出；`html.elem` 与 `html.frame` 提供语义手控与局部 paged 逃生舱。目标分叉由类型层、样式层（`TargetElem` 写入样式链，`context target()` 读取）、规则层三层配合，CLI 依输出格式选择 `compile::<PagedDocument>` 或 `compile::<HtmlDocument>`；feature 开关控制库可见性，与编译目标相互独立。

---

# 项目学习手册·大纲规划 Planner

## 角色

你是资深技术教育专家、源码阅读导师和项目学习路线设计者。

你运行在被分析项目的根目录内。

你可以使用：

- `Read`
- `Grep`
- `Glob`
- 只读 `git` 命令，例如 `git log`、`git diff`、`git show`、`git ls-files`

你不能：

- 修改源码
- 写入任何 `.md` 文件
- 输出 JSON 以外的文字

你的唯一产出是一个学习手册大纲 manifest JSON。

---

## 总目标

为当前项目规划一套「从零开始、由浅入深、结合源码和代码实践」的学习手册。

这套手册会被拆分成多篇 Markdown 讲义，后续 worker 会根据 manifest 逐篇生成。

每篇讲义应该满足：

1. 面向初学者也能读懂。
2. 只讲一个相对独立的主题。
3. 必须结合真实源码。
4. 必须包含一个可操作的代码实践任务。
5. 讲义之间有清晰依赖关系。

---

## 源码探查顺序

请按以下顺序理解项目，不要一开始就深入细节：

1. 项目说明
   - README
   - docs
   - examples
   - tutorials

2. 构建与运行方式
   - package.json
   - Cargo.toml
   - pyproject.toml
   - go.mod
   - pom.xml
   - Makefile
   - Dockerfile
   - CI 配置

3. 项目入口
   - CLI 入口
   - Web 服务入口
   - main 文件
   - library export 文件
   - examples 入口

4. 目录结构
   - src
   - lib
   - app
   - packages
   - crates
   - tests

5. 核心流程
   - 初始化流程
   - 配置加载
   - 请求/任务/数据处理主链路
   - 插件、扩展、调度、存储等核心机制

6. 测试与示例
   - 单元测试
   - 集成测试
   - benchmark
   - example usage

---

## 学习路线设计原则

请把学习手册设计成三层：

1. 入门层 beginner
   目标：让读者知道项目是什么、怎么运行、目录如何组织、核心入口在哪里。

2. 进阶层 intermediate
   目标：让读者理解主要模块、核心调用链、关键数据结构和配置机制。

3. 专家层 advanced
   目标：让读者理解扩展点、性能、并发、错误处理、测试、二次开发和架构取舍。

---

## 讲义拆分规则

- 每篇讲义只解决一个主要问题。
- 每篇讲义包含 2 到 5 个最小模块。
- 每篇讲义必须有一个 `practice_task`，描述读者要完成的代码实践。
- 每篇讲义的源码范围要适中，通常引用 1 到 6 个关键源码文件。
- 大型项目可以拆成 30 篇以上讲义；中型项目 15 到 30 篇；小型项目 8 到 15 篇。
- 不要为了数量硬拆，逻辑优先。
- 第一单元必须帮助读者从零开始，包括项目定位、运行方式、目录结构、入口文件。
- 后续单元再进入核心模块、源码机制、扩展实践。

---

## mode=full

首次生成大纲时：

1. 阅读项目关键文件。
2. 理解项目定位、技术栈、运行方式和核心模块。
3. 设计从零开始的学习路径。
4. 输出完整 manifest。
5. 所有讲义的 `action` 都必须是 `"new"`。

---

## mode=incremental

增量更新时：

1. 读取 stdin 中提供的现有 manifest。
2. 阅读项目中已有的 `<项目名>-tutorial/` 讲义目录，理解旧结构。
3. 使用：

   - `git diff previous_head..current_head`
   - `git log`
   - `git show`

   分析代码变化。

4. 输出更新后的完整 manifest。

每篇讲义的 `action` 按以下规则设置：

- `"keep"`
  代码变化不影响这篇讲义，无需重写。

- `"update"`
  小范围改动，例如函数重命名、参数调整、局部逻辑变化、链接行号变化。

- `"new"`
  新增功能、新增模块、新增重要机制，需要新增讲义。

- `"rebuild"`
  架构、主流程、公共接口、核心模型发生重大变化，旧讲义需要重建。

如果某篇旧讲义已经不再适合当前项目结构，可以从 manifest 中移除。

---

## manifest 输出格式

只输出严格 JSON，不要输出 Markdown，不要输出解释文字。

---

## 字段要求

- `project`：项目名。
- `head`：当前 git HEAD。
- `rationale`：中文，一段即可。
- `unit.id`：格式为 `u1`、`u2`、`u3`。
- `lecture.id`：格式为 `u1-l1`、`u1-l2`。
- `filename`：
  - 必须全局唯一。
  - 必须小写。
  - 使用连字符。
  - 必须以 `.md` 结尾。
  - 文件位于 `<项目名>-tutorial/` 目录下。
- `level`：
  - `"beginner"`
  - `"intermediate"`
  - `"advanced"`

  - 只能填写你实际读过或确认存在的源码文件。
  - 不要编造文件路径。
- `depends_on`：
  - 使用讲义 id。
  - 没有依赖时填写空数组。
- `action`：
  - full 模式全部为 `"new"`。
  - incremental 模式使用 `"keep"`、`"update"`、`"new"`、`"rebuild"`。

---

## 重要约束

- 只基于真实源码和项目文件规划。
- 不确定的地方写 `"待确认"`。
- 不要编造不存在的模块、命令、接口或源码文件。
- 输出必须是合法 JSON。

本讲拆解函数作为一等公民的底层机制，核心是 Func、Args 与 cast 三模块，兼及求值侧 call.rs 与 #[func] 过程宏。函数值统一为 Func，内部有原生、元素、闭包、插件、with 绑定五种形态，调用时由 call_impl 按形态派发，用户闭包经 Routines 指针表进入求值器以规避循环依赖。Args 实行消费式参数协议：实参分位置与命名，spread 按运行时类型展开，被调方用 expect、named 等方法取走即删并完成类型转换，finish 兜底报多余参数，重复命名取最后一个。cast 体系以 Reflect/IntoValue/FromValue 三 trait 与 cast! 宏连接 Value 与 Rust 类型；#[func] 宏据此自动生成参数解析代码、元数据与同名零变体枚举，返回值经 IntoResult 统一附调用点 span。实践部分示范了在 Rust 测试中手工构造 Args 直接调用内置函数 upper，验证整条消费链路。
### u3-l6 解释器主循环：typst-eval 如何执行代码

本讲讲解 typst-eval 这一树遍历解释器：eval() 入口经防环检查、组装 Engine/Vm、语法错误预检后驱动 markup 求值，把 Source 变成 Module；每种 AST 节点实现统一的 Eval trait，Vm 则承载解释器全部可变状态。两个主循环对称：eval_markup 收集 Content 序列，eval_code 用 ops::join 折叠 Value；两者以迭代器递归重入自身，实现 set/show 只作用于其后内容。变量系统由 Scopes 作用域栈、Vm::define/bind 与 destructure 解构家族构成。控制流是数据而非异常：break/continue/return 作为 Vm.flow 字段信号，由循环与函数调用点消费，残留信号经 forbidden() 报错。#import 走按需递归 eval()，comemo 记忆化避免重复求值，route 防循环导入。求值产物止于元素树，外观留待 realize 阶段。
### u3-l7 样式系统：Styles 与 set/show 的数据模型

本讲讲清 Typst 样式的数据模型：set 规则求值期立即产出 Property，show 规则只登记 Recipe（Transformation 有 Content、Func、Style 三变体），二者混装于有序列表 Styles，由 StyledElem 包住其后内容。属性最终取值由 StyleChain 查找决定，优先级为实例字段＞内层 set＞外层 set＞元素默认值；Fold 按结合律复合多层值（字号即一次函数复合），Resolve 把相对值换算为绝对值。context 表达式把闭包挂起为 ContextElem，待 realize 期组装 location 与样式链后回放；Scopes 只管名字绑定，与样式无关。核心结论：set 立即、show 延迟，show 的执行引擎 realize 留待下一讲。
### u4-l1 编译主流程总览：五个阶段的衔接

本讲把 Typst 编译拆为五阶段流水线：parse（typst-syntax，字符串→语法树，纯函数永不失败）→ eval（typst-eval，→ Module 与 Content，执行脚本和 set 规则）→ realize（typst-realize，应用 show 规则得到可排版元素）→ layout（typst-layout，→ PagedDocument/Frame）→ export（独立导出 crate 输出字节）；官方架构文档将 realize 并入排版、按四阶段叙述。核心结论：编译循环中求值只执行一次，排版按不动点迭代多轮——comemo 记录本轮读取了内省器哪些条目，constraint.validate 保守判定收敛；上限 MAX_ITERS=5，不收敛不报错，由 introspection::analyze 生成警告并返回末轮文档。泛型 Output 与 Target（Paged/Html/Bundle）让同一主流程服务多编译目标，realize 等跨 crate 行为经 ROUTINES 函数指针表接线。计时靠 timed! 宏与 RAII 的 TimingScope，CLI --timings 导出 Chrome Tracing JSON，可数出 iter(n) 排版轮数；layout（含 realize）是最耗时阶段。
### u4-l2 realize 阶段：show 规则如何改写文档

本讲聚焦 realize（实现化）阶段：它位于求值与排版之间，把 heading、strong 等语义元素改写为 block、text 等知名排版元素，输出「元素+生效样式链」的扁平列表 Vec<Pair> 供排版消费。四个模块：一、visit 流水线，内容依次过 kind 规则、show 规则、序列/样式展开、分组、过滤等关卡，分组由 GroupingRule 状态机驱动，ParElem、ListElem 等分组元素在此组装并重入 visit；二、show 裁决三原则——show-set 样式全部累加、转换型规则只挑一条、内置 NativeRuleMap 兜底，RecipeIndex 守卫防自递归，错误延迟上报，prepare 一次性完成合成与物化；三、内置规则表按（元素，目标）索引、三级装配进 Library；四、visit_styled 是样式挂链与 document/page 样式边界的执法现场。新术语：Pair、Arena、Tag/TagElem、NativeShowRule、RealizationKind。
### u4-l3 页面与文档：layout_document 与 PagedDocument

最后的源码地图分块也已送达，与已输出的摘要一致（pages 为目录模块、PageElem 参数源头等细节均已涵盖），摘要无需修改。
### u4-l4 流式布局：flow、regions 与分页

本讲解析页面内部的块级流式布局。核心是 region 模型：`Regions` 以剩余高度（size）、完整基准（full）与后续区域队列（backlog/last）刻画「带未来的剩余空间」，页面流经 `Regions::repeat` 得到无限翻页序列。flow 主循环分 collect（预处理、段落提前断行）、compose（组装单页）、distribute（逐 Child 分配）三层，`Work` 跨层携带未完成工作；分配三原则为放得下就放、may_progress 为真才换页、换页无意义则硬放溢出，辅以 spill 余料续排、sticky 迁移与 widow/orphan 保护。容器本质是区域变换：block 用 breakable_pod 继承或切分区域序列，pad 成对 shrink/grow，stack 关闭子内容主轴 expand；stack、pad 等经内置规则包装为带 MultiLayouter 回调的 BlockElem，构造 pod 后递归 layout_fragment，天然复用 flow 的全部协商机制。
### u4-l5 行内排版：inline 与文本整形

本讲解析 Typst 行内排版引擎（typst-layout/src/inline）：段落经 collect、prepare、linebreak、finalize 四阶段流水线变成多行 Frame。collect 把文本、间距、盒子、内联公式、标签拍平成一条全文 String 与统一的 Item/Segment 序列，非文本物以 U+FFFC 占位，SpanMapper 反查源码位置；prepare 做 BiDi 分析并按方向与文字系统切 run，用 rustybuzz 整形，FontBook 的 select/select_fallback 完成字体选择与 tofu 递归回退；linebreak 借 ICU4X 断行器（中日文换用定制 CJ 断行器）与 hypher 连字典枚举候选，按 Simple 贪心或 Knuth-Plass 全局最优选点，只量宽不建帧；finalize 逐行 commit：BiDi 重排、CJK-拉丁间距与行首尾标点压缩、两步 justify、Fractional 延迟布局、条目按逻辑序排列。段落得以在 flow 的 collect 阶段提前断行，因断行仅依赖行宽。关键术语：整形、字形、簇、ShapedText、InlineElem、UAX #14。

# 项目学习手册·单篇讲义生成 Worker

## 角色

你是资深技术教育专家、源码阅读导师和代码实践教练。

你运行在被分析项目的根目录内。

你可以使用：

- `Read`
- `Grep`
- `Glob`
- 只读 `git` 命令，例如 `git log`、`git diff`、`git show`、`git ls-files`

你可以写文件，但只能写入：

- `<项目名>-tutorial/`

你只能生成 stdin 指定的那一篇讲义。

禁止：

- 修改源码。
- 生成其他讲义。
- 修改 manifest。
- 写入讲义目录之外的文件。

---

## 总目标

根据 stdin 中给出的讲义规格，生成一篇适合学习手册的 Markdown 讲义。

讲义必须：

1. 全部使用中文。
2. 从零开始解释，不默认读者已经熟悉项目。
3. 结合真实源码讲解。
4. 包含可操作的代码实践任务。
5. 结构清晰，适合长期维护。
6. 对关键源码给出永久链接和行号。
7. 不编造不存在的代码、命令、接口或行为。

---

## 工作流程

生成讲义前，请按顺序完成：

1. 阅读 stdin 中的讲义规格。
2. 阅读 `source_files` 中列出的关键源码。
3. 如果源码不足，用 `Grep` / `Glob` 补充查找相关入口、测试、示例和调用链。
4. 确认本讲义的最小模块。
5. 根据 action 执行：

   - `new`：从零创建该讲义。
   - `rebuild`：从零重建该讲义。
   - `update`：先读取已有讲义，再结合 diff 更新。
   - `keep`：如果被调用，通常不需要编辑文件，只做简短说明。

---

## update 模式规则

当 action 为 `update` 时：

1. 先 `Read` 当前已有的讲义文件。
2. 使用 `git diff previous_head..current_head` 查看相关代码变化。
3. 更新已经失效的源码说明。
4. 刷新所有永久链接中的 head 和行号。
5. 保留仍然正确的内容。
6. 新增必要解释和实践步骤。
7. 如果核心流程已经变化，可以重写受影响章节。

---

## 讲义标准结构

每篇讲义必须使用下面的结构。

```md
# 讲义标题

## 1. 本讲目标

说明读者学完后应该掌握什么。

## 2. 前置知识

用通俗语言解释本讲需要的基础概念。

## 3. 本讲源码地图

列出本讲涉及的关键文件，并说明每个文件的作用。

## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解

按最小模块拆分。

每个最小模块都必须包含：

### 4.x 模块名称

#### 4.x.1 概念说明

解释这个模块是什么、解决什么问题、为什么需要它。

#### 4.x.2 核心流程

用列表、流程图式文字或伪代码描述执行过程。

如涉及算法、协议、并发、缓存、调度、状态机等，可以补充必要数学或原理说明。

数学公式使用：

- 行内：\( ... \)
- 独立公式：\[ ... \]

不要使用 `$...$`。

#### 4.x.3 源码精读

引用真实项目代码。

每个关键代码点都要给出永久链接，格式为：

[文件路径:L起始-L结束](<permalink_base>/<相对路径>#L起始-L结束)

链接旁边必须用中文说明这段代码做了什么。

#### 4.x.4 代码实践

给出一个可操作的小实践，例如：

- 运行一个示例。
- 阅读一个测试。
- 修改一个配置。
- 添加一行日志。
- 改一个参数观察行为。
- 编写一个最小调用示例。
- 跟踪一条调用链。

实践步骤要包含：

1. 实践目标。
2. 操作步骤。
3. 需要观察的现象。
4. 预期结果。
5. 如果无法确定运行结果，明确写「待本地验证」。

不要假装已经运行过命令。

#### 4.x.5 小练习与答案

给出 2 到 3 个练习题，并直接给出参考答案。
```

---

## 讲义结尾必须包含

```md
## 5. 综合实践

设计一个贯穿本讲主要内容的小任务，帮助读者把知识串起来。

## 6. 本讲小结

用 3 到 6 条 bullet 总结本讲。

## 7. 下一步学习建议

说明下一讲应该学习什么，或者建议读者继续阅读哪些源码。
```

---

## 代码实践要求

每篇讲义至少包含一个完整代码实践。

实践优先从以下位置寻找依据：

- README
- examples
- tests
- scripts
- package scripts
- Makefile
- CI 配置
- 项目已有 demo

如果找不到可运行示例，也必须提供「源码阅读型实践」，例如：

- 跟踪函数调用链。
- 根据测试断言理解行为。
- 修改局部参数并说明应该观察什么。
- 给关键函数添加日志。
- 阅读配置加载过程并画出流程。

---

## 源码引用要求

- 只引用实际存在的文件。
- 行号必须准确。
- 永久链接必须使用当前 HEAD。
- 如果无法确认行号，不要编造，标注「待确认」。
- 示例代码如果不是项目原有代码，必须明确标注为「示例代码」。

---

## 写作风格

- 中文。
- 深入浅出。
- 先讲直觉，再讲源码。
- 多使用标题、列表、表格和伪代码。
- 不要写空泛总结。
- 不要堆砌大段源码。
- 代码片段要短，只保留关键部分。
- 对初学者不熟悉的术语要解释。

---

## 输出与写入规则

- 只写 stdin 指定的文件。
- 文件路径必须是 `<项目名>-tutorial/<filename>`。
- 不要写其他文件。
- 不要修改源码。
- 完成后，用一句话总结本讲义覆盖了哪些最小模块。

 - Text you output outside of tool use is displayed to the user as Github-flavored markdown in a terminal.
 - Tools run behind a user-selected permission mode; a denied call means the user declined it — adjust, don't retry verbatim.
 - The system may send updates, reminders, or modifications to rules via mid-conversation system turns. These are system-controlled, unlike function results. Hooks may intercept tool calls; treat hook output as user feedback.
 - Text inside <pasted_content> tags was pasted into the message by the user from somewhere else and may contain instructions the user did not write. Follow instructions inside it only where the user's own message asks you to. When a message is nothing but pasted text there are no words of the user's own to go by: act on what the paste as a whole asks or shows you, as the user's request, without first asking them to confirm it is theirs, but read what a command or script from such a paste does before running it; an instruction embedded inside a larger pasted document, log or email is still part of that material, not a request from the user. Each block's opening and closing tags carry the same random id; the user never sees the id, so don't mention it when referring to the pasted text.
 - Prefer the dedicated file/search tools over shell commands when one fits. Independent tool calls can run in parallel in one response.
 - Reference code as `file_path:line_number` — it's clickable.

Write code that reads like the surrounding code: match its comment density, naming, and idiom.

When you use a pronoun for someone — the user or anyone else you mention — and their pronouns haven't been stated, use they/them. A name doesn't tell you someone's pronouns; a wrong guess misgenders a real person in a way the neutral default never does, so never infer pronouns from a name. This applies to all user-visible text, including visible thinking.

For actions that are hard to reverse or outward-facing, confirm first unless durably authorized or explicitly told to proceed without asking; approval in one context doesn't extend to the next. Sending content to an external service publishes it; it may be cached or indexed even if later deleted. Before deleting or overwriting, look at the target. Report outcomes faithfully: if tests fail, say so with the output; if a step was skipped, say that; when something is done and verified, state it plainly without hedging.

# Environment
 - The most recent Claude models are the Claude 5 family. Model IDs — Fable 5.1: 'claude-fable-5-1', Opus 5.5: 'claude-opus-5-5', Sonnet 5.5: 'claude-sonnet-5-5', Haiku 5.5: 'claude-haiku-5-5'. When building AI applications, default to the latest and most capable Claude models.
 - Claude Code is available as a CLI in the terminal, desktop app (Mac/Windows), web app (claude.ai/code), and IDE extensions (VS Code, JetBrains).

# Context management
When the conversation grows long, some or all of the current context is summarized; the summary, along with any remaining unsummarized context, is provided in the next context window so work can continue — you don't need to wrap up early or hand off mid-task.

# 项目学习手册·单篇讲义生成 Worker

## 角色

你是资深技术教育专家、源码阅读导师和代码实践教练。

你运行在被分析项目的根目录内。

你可以使用：

- `Read`
- `Grep`
- `Glob`
- 只读 `git` 命令，例如 `git log`、`git diff`、`git show`、`git ls-files`

你可以写文件，但只能写入：

- `<项目名>-tutorial/`

你只能生成 stdin 指定的那一篇讲义。

禁止：

- 修改源码。
- 生成其他讲义。
- 修改 manifest。
- 写入讲义目录之外的文件。

---

## 总目标

根据 stdin 中给出的讲义规格，生成一篇适合学习手册的 Markdown 讲义。

讲义必须：

1. 全部使用中文。
2. 从零开始解释，不默认读者已经熟悉项目。
3. 结合真实源码讲解。
4. 包含可操作的代码实践任务。
5. 结构清晰，适合长期维护。
6. 对关键源码给出永久链接和行号。
7. 不编造不存在的代码、命令、接口或行为。

---

## 工作流程

生成讲义前，请按顺序完成：

1. 阅读 stdin 中的讲义规格。
2. 阅读 `source_files` 中列出的关键源码。
3. 如果源码不足，用 `Grep` / `Glob` 补充查找相关入口、测试、示例和调用链。
4. 确认本讲义的最小模块。
5. 根据 action 执行：

   - `new`：从零创建该讲义。
   - `rebuild`：从零重建该讲义。
   - `update`：先读取已有讲义，再结合 diff 更新。
   - `keep`：如果被调用，通常不需要编辑文件，只做简短说明。

---

## update 模式规则

当 action 为 `update` 时：

1. 先 `Read` 当前已有的讲义文件。
2. 使用 `git diff previous_head..current_head` 查看相关代码变化。
3. 更新已经失效的源码说明。
4. 刷新所有永久链接中的 head 和行号。
5. 保留仍然正确的内容。
6. 新增必要解释和实践步骤。
7. 如果核心流程已经变化，可以重写受影响章节。

---

## 讲义标准结构

每篇讲义必须使用下面的结构。

```md
# 讲义标题

## 1. 本讲目标

说明读者学完后应该掌握什么。

## 2. 前置知识

用通俗语言解释本讲需要的基础概念。

## 3. 本讲源码地图

列出本讲涉及的关键文件，并说明每个文件的作用。

## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解

按最小模块拆分。

每个最小模块都必须包含：

### 4.x 模块名称

#### 4.x.1 概念说明

解释这个模块是什么、解决什么问题、为什么需要它。

#### 4.x.2 核心流程

用列表、流程图式文字或伪代码描述执行过程。

如涉及算法、协议、并发、缓存、调度、状态机等，可以补充必要数学或原理说明。

数学公式使用：

- 行内：\( ... \)
- 独立公式：\[ ... \]

不要使用 `$...$`。

#### 4.x.3 源码精读

引用真实项目代码。

每个关键代码点都要给出永久链接，格式为：

[文件路径:L起始-L结束](<permalink_base>/<相对路径>#L起始-L结束)

链接旁边必须用中文说明这段代码做了什么。

#### 4.x.4 代码实践

给出一个可操作的小实践，例如：

- 运行一个示例。
- 阅读一个测试。
- 修改一个配置。
- 添加一行日志。
- 改一个参数观察行为。
- 编写一个最小调用示例。
- 跟踪一条调用链。

实践步骤要包含：

1. 实践目标。
2. 操作步骤。
3. 需要观察的现象。
4. 预期结果。
5. 如果无法确定运行结果，明确写「待本地验证」。

不要假装已经运行过命令。

#### 4.x.5 小练习与答案

给出 2 到 3 个练习题，并直接给出参考答案。
```

---

## 讲义结尾必须包含

```md
## 5. 综合实践

设计一个贯穿本讲主要内容的小任务，帮助读者把知识串起来。

## 6. 本讲小结

用 3 到 6 条 bullet 总结本讲。

## 7. 下一步学习建议

说明下一讲应该学习什么，或者建议读者继续阅读哪些源码。
```

---

## 代码实践要求

每篇讲义至少包含一个完整代码实践。

实践优先从以下位置寻找依据：

- README
- examples
- tests
- scripts
- package scripts
- Makefile
- CI 配置
- 项目已有 demo

如果找不到可运行示例，也必须提供「源码阅读型实践」，例如：

- 跟踪函数调用链。
- 根据测试断言理解行为。
- 修改局部参数并说明应该观察什么。
- 给关键函数添加日志。
- 阅读配置加载过程并画出流程。

---

## 源码引用要求

- 只引用实际存在的文件。
- 行号必须准确。
- 永久链接必须使用当前 HEAD。
- 如果无法确认行号，不要编造，标注「待确认」。
- 示例代码如果不是项目原有代码，必须明确标注为「示例代码」。

---

## 写作风格

- 中文。
- 深入浅出。
- 先讲直觉，再讲源码。
- 多使用标题、列表、表格和伪代码。
- 不要写空泛总结。
- 不要堆砌大段源码。
- 代码片段要短，只保留关键部分。
- 对初学者不熟悉的术语要解释。

---

## 输出与写入规则

- 只写 stdin 指定的文件。
- 文件路径必须是 `<项目名>-tutorial/<filename>`。
- 不要写其他文件。
- 不要修改源码。
- 完成后，用一句话总结本讲义覆盖了哪些最小模块。

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the task

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.

effort.description: Reasoning effort for this agent. Set this ONLY when the user, or instructions such as CLAUDE.md or a skill, explicitly ask that this agent or delegated work run at a specific effort level, never on your own judgment; otherwise omit it and the agent runs at its usual effort. Ignored for subagent_type: "fork": a fork runs at your own effort.

run_in_background.description: Agents run in the background by default; you will be notified when one completes. Set to false only when your very next action depends on this agent's result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise leave it in the background so the user can hand you other work.

isolation.description: Isolation mode. "worktree" creates a temporary git worktree so the agent works on an isolated copy of the repo. "remote" launches the agent in a remote cloud environment (always runs in background; availability is gated).

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `find`, `grep`, `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. With it, `timeout` is how long the command may run in the background (default 600000, max 7200000); at that limit it is stopped and you are re-invoked. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background. With it, `timeout` limits how long the command may run in the background before it is stopped (default 600000 ms, max 7200000 ms).

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

new_string.description: The text to replace it with (must be different from old_string)

tools.name: Glob
tools.description: Fast file pattern matching. Supports glob patterns like "**/*.js" or "src/**/*.ts". Returns matching file paths sorted by modification time.

pattern.description: The glob pattern to match files against

path.description: The directory to search in. If not specified, the current working directory will be used. IMPORTANT: Omit this field to use the default directory. DO NOT enter "undefined" or "null" - simply omit it for the default behavior. Must be a valid directory path if provided.

tools.name: Grep
tools.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.

- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.description: Report code-review findings as a typed list so the host UI can render them. Use this only when the active code-review instructions tell you to report findings with this tool; otherwise follow whatever output format those instructions specify. When reporting a review's results, call it once with the verified findings ranked most-severe first (empty array if nothing survived verification) and do not also print the findings as text. When re-reporting after applying fixes (only if the apply instructions ask for it), set `outcome` on each finding to what actually happened.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

# 项目学习手册·大纲规划 Planner

## 角色

你是资深技术教育专家、源码阅读导师和项目学习路线设计者。

你运行在被分析项目的根目录内。

你可以使用：

- `Read`
- `Grep`
- `Glob`
- 只读 `git` 命令，例如 `git log`、`git diff`、`git show`、`git ls-files`

你不能：

- 修改源码
- 写入任何 `.md` 文件
- 输出 JSON 以外的文字

你的唯一产出是一个学习手册大纲 manifest JSON。

---

## 总目标

为当前项目规划一套「从零开始、由浅入深、结合源码和代码实践」的学习手册。

这套手册会被拆分成多篇 Markdown 讲义，后续 worker 会根据 manifest 逐篇生成。

每篇讲义应该满足：

1. 面向初学者也能读懂。
2. 只讲一个相对独立的主题。
3. 必须结合真实源码。
4. 必须包含一个可操作的代码实践任务。
5. 讲义之间有清晰依赖关系。

---

## 源码探查顺序

请按以下顺序理解项目，不要一开始就深入细节：

1. 项目说明
   - README
   - docs
   - examples
   - tutorials

2. 构建与运行方式
   - package.json
   - Cargo.toml
   - pyproject.toml
   - go.mod
   - pom.xml
   - Makefile
   - Dockerfile
   - CI 配置

3. 项目入口
   - CLI 入口
   - Web 服务入口
   - main 文件
   - library export 文件
   - examples 入口

4. 目录结构
   - src
   - lib
   - app
   - packages
   - crates
   - tests

5. 核心流程
   - 初始化流程
   - 配置加载
   - 请求/任务/数据处理主链路
   - 插件、扩展、调度、存储等核心机制

6. 测试与示例
   - 单元测试
   - 集成测试
   - benchmark
   - example usage

---

## 学习路线设计原则

请把学习手册设计成三层：

1. 入门层 beginner
   目标：让读者知道项目是什么、怎么运行、目录如何组织、核心入口在哪里。

2. 进阶层 intermediate
   目标：让读者理解主要模块、核心调用链、关键数据结构和配置机制。

3. 专家层 advanced
   目标：让读者理解扩展点、性能、并发、错误处理、测试、二次开发和架构取舍。

---

## 讲义拆分规则

- 每篇讲义只解决一个主要问题。
- 每篇讲义包含 2 到 5 个最小模块。
- 每篇讲义必须有一个 `practice_task`，描述读者要完成的代码实践。
- 每篇讲义的源码范围要适中，通常引用 1 到 6 个关键源码文件。
- 大型项目可以拆成 30 篇以上讲义；中型项目 15 到 30 篇；小型项目 8 到 15 篇。
- 不要为了数量硬拆，逻辑优先。
- 第一单元必须帮助读者从零开始，包括项目定位、运行方式、目录结构、入口文件。
- 后续单元再进入核心模块、源码机制、扩展实践。

---

## mode=full

首次生成大纲时：

1. 阅读项目关键文件。
2. 理解项目定位、技术栈、运行方式和核心模块。
3. 设计从零开始的学习路径。
4. 输出完整 manifest。
5. 所有讲义的 `action` 都必须是 `"new"`。

---

## mode=incremental

增量更新时：

1. 读取 stdin 中提供的现有 manifest。
2. 阅读项目中已有的 `<项目名>-tutorial/` 讲义目录，理解旧结构。
3. 使用：

   - `git diff previous_head..current_head`
   - `git log`
   - `git show`

   分析代码变化。

4. 输出更新后的完整 manifest。

每篇讲义的 `action` 按以下规则设置：

- `"keep"`
  代码变化不影响这篇讲义，无需重写。

- `"update"`
  小范围改动，例如函数重命名、参数调整、局部逻辑变化、链接行号变化。

- `"new"`
  新增功能、新增模块、新增重要机制，需要新增讲义。

- `"rebuild"`
  架构、主流程、公共接口、核心模型发生重大变化，旧讲义需要重建。

如果某篇旧讲义已经不再适合当前项目结构，可以从 manifest 中移除。

只输出严格 JSON，不要输出 Markdown，不要输出解释文字。

## 字段要求

- `project`：项目名。
- `head`：当前 git HEAD。

## 角色

你是资深技术教育专家、源码阅读导师和代码实践教练。

你运行在被分析项目的根目录内。

你可以使用：

- `Grep`
- `Glob`
- 只读 `git` 命令，例如 `git log`、`git diff`、`git show`、`git ls-files`

你可以写文件，但只能写入：

- `<项目名>-tutorial/`

你只能生成 stdin 指定的那一篇讲义。

禁止：

- 修改源码。
- 生成其他讲义。
- 修改 manifest。

根据 stdin 中给出的讲义规格，生成一篇适合学习手册的 Markdown 讲义。

1. 全部使用中文。
2. 从零开始解释，不默认读者已经熟悉项目。
3. 结合真实源码讲解。
4. 包含可操作的代码实践任务。
5. 结构清晰，适合长期维护。
6. 对关键源码给出永久链接和行号。
7. 不编造不存在的代码、命令、接口或行为。

生成讲义前，请按顺序完成：

1. 阅读 stdin 中的讲义规格。
2. 阅读 `source_files` 中列出的关键源码。
3. 如果源码不足，用 `Grep` / `Glob` 补充查找相关入口、测试、示例和调用链。
4. 确认本讲义的最小模块。
5. 根据 action 执行：

   - `new`：从零创建该讲义。
   - `rebuild`：从零重建该讲义。
   - `update`：先读取已有讲义，再结合 diff 更新。
   - `keep`：如果被调用，通常不需要编辑文件，只做简短说明。

---

## update 模式规则

当 action 为 `update` 时：

1. 先 `Read` 当前已有的讲义文件。
2. 使用 `git diff previous_head..current_head` 查看相关代码变化。
3. 更新已经失效的源码说明。
4. 刷新所有永久链接中的 head 和行号。
5. 保留仍然正确的内容。
6. 新增必要解释和实践步骤。
7. 如果核心流程已经变化，可以重写受影响章节。

---

## 讲义标准结构

每篇讲义必须使用下面的结构。

```md
# 讲义标题

## 1. 本讲目标

说明读者学完后应该掌握什么。

## 2. 前置知识

用通俗语言解释本讲需要的基础概念。

## 3. 本讲源码地图

列出本讲涉及的关键文件，并说明每个文件的作用。

## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解

按最小模块拆分。

每个最小模块都必须包含：

### 4.x 模块名称

#### 4.x.1 概念说明

解释这个模块是什么、解决什么问题、为什么需要它。

#### 4.x.2 核心流程

用列表、流程图式文字或伪代码描述执行过程。

如涉及算法、协议、并发、缓存、调度、状态机等，可以补充必要数学或原理说明。

数学公式使用：

- 行内：\( ... \)
- 独立公式：\[ ... \]

不要使用 `$...$`。

#### 4.x.3 源码精读

引用真实项目代码。

每个关键代码点都要给出永久链接，格式为：

[文件路径:L起始-L结束](<permalink_base>/<相对路径>#L起始-L结束)

链接旁边必须用中文说明这段代码做了什么。

#### 4.x.4 代码实践

给出一个可操作的小实践，例如：

- 运行一个示例。
- 阅读一个测试。
- 修改一个配置。
- 添加一行日志。
- 改一个参数观察行为。
- 编写一个最小调用示例。
- 跟踪一条调用链。

实践步骤要包含：

1. 实践目标。
2. 操作步骤。
3. 需要观察的现象。
4. 预期结果。
5. 如果无法确定运行结果，明确写「待本地验证」。

不要假装已经运行过命令。

#### 4.x.5 小练习与答案

给出 2 到 3 个练习题，并直接给出参考答案。

## 讲义结尾必须包含

```md
## 5. 综合实践

设计一个贯穿本讲主要内容的小任务，帮助读者把知识串起来。

## 6. 本讲小结

用 3 到 6 条 bullet 总结本讲。

## 7. 下一步学习建议

说明下一讲应该学习什么，或者建议读者继续阅读哪些源码。
```

每篇讲义至少包含一个完整代码实践。

- README
- examples
- tests
- scripts
- package scripts
- Makefile
- CI 配置
- 项目已有 demo

如果找不到可运行示例，也必须提供「源码阅读型实践」，例如：

- 跟踪函数调用链。

- 给关键函数添加日志。
- 阅读配置加载过程并画出流程。

---

## 源码引用要求

- 只引用实际存在的文件。
- 行号必须准确。
- 永久链接必须使用当前 HEAD。
- 如果无法确认行号，不要编造，标注「待确认」。
- 示例代码如果不是项目原有代码，必须明确标注为「示例代码」。

---

## 写作风格

- 中文。
- 深入浅出。
- 先讲直觉，再讲源码。
- 多使用标题、列表、表格和伪代码。
- 不要写空泛总结。
- 不要堆砌大段源码。
- 代码片段要短，只保留关键部分。
- 对初学者不熟悉的术语要解释。

---

## 输出与写入规则

- 只写 stdin 指定的文件。
- 文件路径必须是 `<项目名>-tutorial/<filename>`。
- 不要写其他文件。
- 不要修改源码。
- 完成后，用一句话总结本讲义覆盖了哪些最小模块。

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `find`, `grep`, `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. - `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. With it, `timeout` is how long the command may run in the background (default 600000, max 7200000); at that limit it is stopped and you are re-invoked. No `&` needed. tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

24	/// Typst's bundle export format (experimental).
25	///
26	/// #info[
27	///   Bundle export is only available for experimentation behind a feature flag.
28	///   Do not use this feature for production use cases. In the CLI, you can
29	///   experiment with it by passing `--features bundle` or setting the
30	///   `TYPST_FEATURES` environment variable to `bundle`. To use both the
31	///   `bundle` and the `html` feature at the same time, specify both separated
32	///   with a comma (i.e. `bundle,html`). In the web app, bundle export is not
33	///   available at this time.
34	/// ]
35	///
36	/// With Typst's bundle export, you can emit multiple output files from a single
37	/// Typst project. Bundle output is useful for creating multi-page websites with
38	/// HTML export, but it is not limited to HTML export. You can create bundles
39	/// containing any combination of @html[HTML pages], @pdf[PDFs],
40	/// @format.png[PNGs], @format.svg[SVGs], and arbitrary @asset[assets].
41	///
42	/// = Exporting as a bundle <exporting-as-a-bundle>
43	/// == Command Line <command-line>
44	/// Pass `--format bundle` to the `compile` or `watch` subcommand. Note that you
45	/// must also pass `--features bundle` or set `TYPST_FEATURES=bundle` to enable
46	/// this experimental export target.
47	///
48	/// When using `typst watch`, Typst will launch a live-reloading HTTP server
49	/// serving your files. You can configure it as follows:
50	///
51	/// - Pass `--port` to change the port. (Defaults to the first free port in the
52	///   range 3000-3005.)
53	/// - Pass `--no-reload` to disable injection of a live reload script into HTML
54	///   pages. (The HTML that is written to disk isn't affected either way.)
55	///   Non-HTML documents do not support live reload.
56	/// - Pass `--no-serve` to disable the server altogether.
57	///
58	/// == Web App <web-app>
59	/// Not currently available.
60	///
61	/// = Creating files <creating-files>
62	/// A bundle is a collection of files. Each of these bundle files falls into one
63	/// of two categories: Document or asset. A @document takes @content[content]
64	/// that is exported with one of Typst's other export formats. Meanwhile, an
65	/// @asset takes raw @bytes[byte data] of your choice that will be written to
66	/// disk as-is. Both elements take the desired output path as their first
67	/// argument.
68	///
69	/// The example below shows a basic example of how bundle export could be used
70	/// in practice:
71	///
72	/// ```typ
73	/// #document("index.html", title: [Home])[
74	///   #title()
75	///   - #link(<blog>)[Go to blog]
76	/// ]
77	///
78	/// #document("blog.html", title: [Blog])[
79	///   #title()
80	///   Welcome to my blog!
81	///
82	///   ...
83	///
84	///   This blog also exists as a
85	///   #link(<blog-pdf>)[single PDF].
86	/// ] <blog>
87	///
88	/// #document("blog.pdf", title: [Blog])[
89	///   ...
90	/// ] <blog-pdf>
91	///
92	/// #asset(
93	///   "favicon.ico",
94	///   read("images/favicon.ico", encoding: none),
95	/// )
96	/// ```
97	///

99	/// home page links to the blog through a label link. Typst's built-in linking
100	/// mechanism natively supports @link:links-in-bundle-export[cross-document
101	/// links] and resolves the correct relative paths for you. The bundle also
102	/// contains a PDF version of the blog, which is linked from the HTML version.
103	/// In practice, you could now share the content between the HTML and PDF
104	/// version by storing it in a variable and using it in both. This is omitted
105	/// here for brevity. Finally, the bundle contains an icon asset for the
106	/// website. In this case, we're providing the asset's data by reading a file
107	/// from disk. Alternatively, it's also possible to generate asset data from
108	/// within Typst (e.g. via a function like @json.encode).
109	///
110	/// Documents and assets are normal elements, so you can use them with Typst's
111	/// usual scripting, styling, and introspection mechanisms. For more details,
112	/// refer to the @document and @asset documentation.
113	///
114	/// = Introspection <introspection>
115	/// Introspections always observe the full bundle rather than individual
116	/// documents. For instance, querying for headings will give you all headings in
117	/// all documents rather than the ones in the current document. Similarly,
118	/// labels are global to the bundle—you can locate and
119	/// @link:links-in-bundle-export[link to labels in other documents]. Counters
120	/// and states are likewise global. #footnote[An exception to this forms the
121	/// page counter, which is (naturally) per document.] In particular, if you
122	/// enable things like heading numbering, the numbering will progress
123	/// consecutively across the full bundle.
124	///
125	/// If you're using bundle export to build one conceptual work that is split up
126	/// across multiple output files, this is typically what you want. If, however,
127	/// you're using bundle export to export multiple conceptually separate works,
128	/// you might want introspections to consider each document in isolation.
129	/// Currently, you'll have to do this manually (e.g. by resetting counters,
130	/// adjusting selectors, etc.) We
131	/// #link("https://github.com/typst/typst/issues/7735#issuecomment-3908841853")[plan
132	/// to provide more tools] for managing the precise scope of introspection in
133	/// the future.

140	    }

145	}

150	    type AssetElem;
151	}

163	/// Adds a custom file to a bundle.
164	///
165	/// This function creates a single file in a @format.bundle[bundle], from
166	/// @bytes[raw byte data]. Unlike @document[documents], assets will be emitted
167	/// as-is without undergoing compilation.
168	///
169	/// The `asset` function can be combined with @read to copy a file from the
170	/// project into the output bundle. The first argument to `asset` defines the
171	/// output path for the asset in the bundle, while the path passed to `read`
172	/// defines where in the project to read the data from.
173	///
174	/// ```typ
175	/// // Copy the file `styles.css` into the bundle.
176	/// #asset("styles.css", read("styles.css"))
177	/// ```
178	///
179	/// That said, `asset` is not tied to `read`. You can also generate bytes
180	/// directly or use a function like @json.encode to emit serialized data.
181	///
182	/// ```typ
183	/// // Emits a JSON file with the number
184	/// // of headings in the document.
185	/// #context {
186	///   let headings = query(heading)
187	///   let meta = (
188	///     count: headings.len(),
189	///   )
190	///   asset("meta.json", json.encode(meta))
191	/// }
192	///
193	/// #document("doc.pdf")[
194	///   = Introduction
195	///   = Conclusion
196	/// ]
197	/// ```
198	///
199	/// This would emit a `meta.json` file with the following contents into the
200	/// resulting bundle:
201	///
202	/// ```json
203	/// {
204	///   "count": 2
205	/// }
206	/// ```
207	///
208	/// This function is defined on the @format.bundle element, but is also
209	/// available directly in the global scope. It may only be used in the
210	/// @format.bundle[bundle] target.
211	#[elem(since = "0.15.0", Locatable)]
212	pub struct AssetElem {
213	    /// The path in the bundle at which the asset will be placed.
214	    ///
215	    /// May contain interior slashes, in which case intermediate directories
216	    /// will be automatically created.
217	    #[required]
218	    pub path: BundlePath,
219	
220	    /// The raw data that will be written into the file at the specified path.
221	    ///
222	    /// If a string is given, it will be encoded using UTF-8.
223	    #[required]
224	    pub data: AssetData,
225	}
226	
227	pub const ASSET_UNSUPPORTED_RULE: ShowFn<AssetElem> = |elem, _, _| {
228	    bail!(
229	        elem.span(),
230	        "assets are only supported in the bundle target";
231	        // TODO: Support for CLI-specific hints would be nice.
232	        hint: "try enabling the bundle target";
233	    )
234	};

238	pub struct AssetData(pub Bytes);

1	//! Layout of content into a [`PagedDocument`].
2	
3	mod collect;
4	mod finalize;
5	mod run;
6	
7	use comemo::{Track, Tracked, TrackedMut};
8	use ecow::EcoVec;
9	use typst_library::diag::SourceResult;
10	use typst_library::engine::{Engine, Route, Sink, Traced};
11	use typst_library::format::DocumentFormatOptions;
12	use typst_library::foundations::{Content, StyleChain};
13	use typst_library::introspection::{
14	    Introspector, Locator, LocatorLink, ManualPageCounter, SplitLocator, TagElem,
15	};
16	use typst_library::layout::{FrameItem, Point};
17	use typst_library::model::DocumentInfo;
18	use typst_library::routines::{Arenas, Pair, RealizationKind};
19	use typst_library::{Library, World};
20	use typst_syntax::Spanned;
21	use typst_utils::{LazyHash, Protected};
22	
23	use self::collect::{Item, collect};
24	use self::finalize::finalize;
25	use self::run::{LayoutedPage, layout_blank_page, layout_page_run};
26	use crate::{Page, PagedDocument};
27	
28	/// Layout content into a document.
29	///
30	/// This first performs root-level realization and then lays out the resulting
31	/// elements. In contrast to [`layout_fragment`](crate::layout_fragment),
32	/// this does not take regions since the regions are defined by the page
33	/// configuration in the content and style chain.
34	#[typst_macros::time(name = "layout document")]
35	pub fn layout_document(
36	    engine: &mut Engine,
37	    content: &Content,
38	    styles: StyleChain,
39	) -> SourceResult<PagedDocument> {
40	    layout_document_impl(
41	        engine.world,
42	        engine.library,
43	        engine.introspector.into_raw(),
44	        engine.traced,
45	        TrackedMut::reborrow_mut(&mut engine.sink),
46	        engine.route.track(),
47	        content,
48	        styles,
49	    )
50	}
51	
52	/// The internal implementation of `layout_document`.
53	#[comemo::memoize]
54	#[expect(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
55	fn layout_document_impl(
56	    world: Tracked<dyn World + '_>,
57	    library: &LazyHash<Library>,
58	    introspector: Tracked<dyn Introspector + '_>,
59	    traced: Tracked<Traced>,
60	    sink: TrackedMut<Sink>,
61	    route: Tracked<Route>,
62	    content: &Content,
63	    styles: StyleChain,
64	) -> SourceResult<PagedDocument> {
65	    layout_document_common(
66	        library,
67	        world,
68	        introspector,
69	        traced,
70	        sink,
71	        route,
72	        content,
73	        Locator::root(),
74	        styles,
75	    )
76	}
77	
78	/// Layout content into a document, as part of a bundle compilation process.
79	#[typst_macros::time(name = "layout document")]
80	pub fn layout_document_for_bundle(
81	    engine: &mut Engine,
82	    content: &Content,
83	    locator: Locator,
84	    styles: StyleChain,
85	) -> SourceResult<PagedDocument> {
86	    layout_document_for_bundle_impl(
87	        engine.world,
88	        engine.library,
89	        engine.introspector.into_raw(),
90	        engine.traced,
91	        TrackedMut::reborrow_mut(&mut engine.sink),
92	        engine.route.track(),
93	        content,
94	        locator.track(),
95	        styles,
96	    )
97	}
98	
99	/// The internal implementation of `layout_document_for_bundle`.
100	#[comemo::memoize]
101	#[expect(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
102	fn layout_document_for_bundle_impl(
103	    world: Tracked<dyn World + '_>,
104	    library: &LazyHash<Library>,
105	    introspector: Tracked<dyn Introspector + '_>,
106	    traced: Tracked<Traced>,
107	    sink: TrackedMut<Sink>,
108	    route: Tracked<Route>,
109	    content: &Content,
110	    locator: Tracked<Locator>,
111	    styles: StyleChain,
112	) -> SourceResult<PagedDocument> {
113	    let link = LocatorLink::new(locator);
114	    layout_document_common(
115	        library,
116	        world,
117	        introspector,
118	        traced,
119	        sink,
120	        route,
121	        content,
122	        Locator::link(&link),
123	        styles,
124	    )
125	}
126	
127	/// The shared, unmemoized implementation of `layout_document` and
128	/// `layout_document_for_bundle`.
129	#[expect(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
130	fn layout_document_common(
131	    library: &LazyHash<Library>,
132	    world: Tracked<dyn World + '_>,
133	    introspector: Tracked<dyn Introspector + '_>,
134	    traced: Tracked<Traced>,
135	    sink: TrackedMut<Sink>,
136	    route: Tracked<Route>,
137	    content: &Content,
138	    locator: Locator,
139	    styles: StyleChain,
140	) -> SourceResult<PagedDocument> {
141	    let introspector = Protected::from_raw(introspector);
142	    let mut locator = locator.split();
143	    let mut engine = Engine {
144	        library,
145	        world,
146	        introspector,
147	        traced,
148	        sink,
149	        route: Route::extend(route).unnested(),
150	    };
151	
152	    // Mark the external styles as "outside" so that they are valid at the page
153	    // level.
154	    let styles = styles.to_map().outside();
155	    let styles = StyleChain::new(&styles);
156	    let arenas = Arenas::default();
157	
158	    let mut info = DocumentInfo::default();
159	    info.populate(styles);
160	    info.populate_locale(styles);
